intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that nephrotic syndrome type 23 (NPHS23) is caused by homozygous mutation in the KIRREL1 gene (607428) on chromosome 1q23.1.

checks.claim: Nephrotic syndrome type 23 (NPHS23) is caused by homozygous mutation in the KIRREL1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe two unrelated families with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with homozygous mutations in the KIRREL1 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous KIRREL1 mutations causing SRNS. 'NPHS23' is a standard disease name and does not appear in the paper.

checks.claim: The KIRREL1 gene is located on chromosome 1q23.1.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing identifies a homozygous mutation of KIRREL1 (p.Arg440Cys) that is positioned within the maximum NPL peak on chromosome 1 (arrowhead).
checks.explanation: The paper places KIRREL1 on chromosome 1 but does not give band 1q23.1. Standard locus nomenclature counts as supported.

paragraphs.text: Nephrotic syndrome type 23 (NPHS23) is an autosomal recessive kidney disorder. Affected individuals have steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) beginning in childhood or adolescence, with proteinuria and no extrarenal features. Renal biopsy shows low-grade mesangial hypercellularity, a picture of minimal change disease or focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, and extensive podocyte foot process effacement. Some patients progress to chronic kidney disease (Solanki et al., 2019).

checks.claim: NPHS23 is an autosomal recessive kidney disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: we have identified and characterized two novel recessive mutations in KIRREL1 gene in two patients with SRNS of 2 unrelated consanguineous families
checks.explanation: Recessive homozygous mutations found in consanguineous families.

paragraphs.text: Solanki et al. (2019) reported a boy (A666_21) from a consanguineous family who was diagnosed with nephrotic syndrome at age 5 years. His nephrotic syndrome was steroid-resistant from the first presentation and did not respond to several immunosuppressive drugs. He never reached complete remission and had undulating proteinuria that responded only partially to treatment. ACE inhibitors and ARBs did not help, but his renal function remained normal over 12.5 years of follow-up. Renal histology showed minor mesangial hypercellularity consistent with minimal change disease. A younger sister reportedly had periorbital edema and proteinuria. Among extended relatives, 3 children had ESRD and 1 had nephrotic syndrome, but none of these relatives had been genotyped.

paragraphs.text: Solanki et al. (2019) stably expressed Flag-tagged KIRREL1 carrying either R440C or S573L in human podocytes. Compared with wildtype, both mutant proteins were mislocalized and reduced in the membrane fraction, with more protein in the Golgi apparatus, early endosomes, and lysosomes. The authors suggested that this pattern reflected trafficking defects. Neither mutation affected the membrane localization of NPHS1. In transepithelial permeability assays, podocyte monolayers expressing mutant KIRREL1 let through significantly more Texas Red-labeled albumin than monolayers expressing wildtype KIRREL1. The authors concluded that the mutations adversely affect podocyte cell junctions and the integrity of contacts between cells.

paragraphs.text: To disrupt the Neph1-nephrin interaction in vivo, Liu et al. (2003) injected rodents with anti-Neph1 and anti-nephrin antibodies together, each at a dose that did not cause nephritis on its own. The animals developed proteinuria that did not depend on complement or leukocytes, and their foot processes were preserved. In podocytes, Neph1 and nephrin protein levels fell modestly and ZO-1 protein fell dramatically, while mRNA levels of all 3 genes were unchanged. The fall in ZO-1 depended on the interaction of ZO-1 PDZ domains with the Neph1 cytoplasmic tail. The authors concluded that the Neph1-nephrin interaction appears to be an important determinant of glomerular permeability.

checks.claim: Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome in patient B742_21 was diagnosed at age 14 years.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient B742_21 was diagnosed with NS at age of 14 years. He developed SRNS at his initial presentation.

checks.claim: Biopsy of patient B742_21 showed focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Renal histology of individual B742_21 with KIRREL1 mutation shows focal segmental glomerular sclerosis (arrows) on light microscopy

checks.claim: The KIRREL1 S573L mutation lay within the maximum homozygosity peak on chromosome 1.
checks.evidence_quote: Within the maximum NPL peak on chromosome 1 (arrowhead), we identified a homozygous mutation in KIRREL1 (p.Ser573Leu).

checks.claim: The KIRREL1 residue altered by S573L is conserved to zebrafish.
checks.evidence_quote: The respective amino acid residues are conserved to D.rerio for both mutations

checks.claim: The KIRREL1 S573L variant had a gnomAD minor allele frequency of 7.87 x 10(-4).
checks.evidence_quote: gnomAD with a minor allele frequency (MAF) of 3.97×10−6 and a MAF of 7.87×10−4 respectively
checks.explanation: The second value refers to p.Ser573Leu.

checks.claim: The KIRREL1 S573L variant was found in the homozygous state in 1 control subject.
checks.evidence_quote: found mutated at the homozygous state in one control subject in GnomAD

checks.claim: Solanki et al. (2019) raised the possibility of variable expressivity or incomplete penetrance for KIRREL1 S573L.
checks.evidence_quote: thus, there is a possibility of variable expressivity or incomplete penetrance for this variant

checks.claim: In human podocytes, KIRREL1 S573L mutant protein was mislocalized and reduced in the membrane fraction.
checks.evidence_quote: the mutant KIRREL1 proteins were present in the membrane fraction at a significant low level.
checks.explanation: Mislocalization of both mutants is also stated.

checks.claim: In human podocytes, more KIRREL1 S573L mutant protein was found in the Golgi apparatus, early endosomes, and lysosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: Both KIRREL1 mutants showed increased localization at Golgi apparatus, early endosomes and lysosomes
